subject: June checkpoint: propose OKR re-scope + QBR prep for BrightCore
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, evelyn.hart@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: June checkpoint: propose OKR re-scope + QBR prep for BrightCore

Team —

Quick mid-quarter checkpoint and a few asks as we prep the July QBR with BrightCore. TL;DR: Serving runtime KRs are at risk because of longer-than-expected kernel integration and slower-than-projected batching gains. I propose a measured re-scope for the quarter to protect delivery on the high-impact items and to give the sales/CS team something stable to present in the QBR.

Status highlights:
- Serving runtime perf (KR: 40% P99 improvement): currently tracking ~18% improvement after recent kernel swaps; integration work on attention optimization is +3 weeks.
- Dedicated capacity autoscaler (KR: production rollout): staging tests stable; production rollout paused pending infra capacity (see below).
- Redwood Optimize recommendations (KR: model pack savings): initial quantization profiles show promise but need 2 more benchmarking passes.

Proposed re-scope (ask for decision by end of day Friday):
1) Convert Serving runtime P99 improvement target from 40% -> 30% for Q3, keep delivery phasing to show incremental wins.
2) Prioritize autoscaler soft-launch (limited regions) rather than wide rollout this quarter.
3) Move exploratory latency-reduction spike (feature spike R-7) to backfill next quarter if infra remains constrained.

Dependency asks (concrete items):
- Infra (Marcus): can we secure an extra DGX node for a 4-week window starting Jul 6 to run long benchmarking sweeps? I attached a DGX_request_form.pdf stub. If DGX not available, please propose fallback (spot GPU pool or cloud burst) and estimated ETA.
- Product (Evelyn): confirm which customer-facing capability we should highlight in the QBR if we re-scope Serving target (option A: autoscaler soft-launch; option B: Optimize quantization wins). Need final pick by Thu EOD so marketing can lock slides.
- CS (Monica): BrightCore expects clear, non-speculative statements in the QBR. Please draft two bullet talking points: one conservative (if we re-scope) and one optimistic (if we hold to original).

Attachments: OKR_rebaseline.xlsx (proposed KR revisions), QBR_slide_deck_v1.pdf (working deck) — both in the Drive link below.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B-OKR-QBR-2026

I'm copying Lauren for prioritization and Steph for any comms implications. If we can't get infra capacity by next week, we need to commit to the re-scope to avoid slipping other teams.

Thanks,
Jonas

Subject: Re: June checkpoint: propose OKR re-scope + QBR prep for BrightCore

Thanks for the clear summary, Jonas. I agree we should avoid overpromising in the QBR. Two quick notes:

1) Approve the temporary re-scope to 30% P99 improvement for the quarter, provided we publish a short roadmap slide showing incremental milestones (week-by-week integration gating).
2) Marcus — if DGX is tight, propose exactly how much cloud burst $$ we'd need for the benchmarking window (estimate in $k). If we can pay to expedite the benchmarks, I'm okay with it for one sprint.

Please make sure the OKR_rebaseline.xlsx has a one-line rationale next to each KR change — that will help sales and execs. Monica, can you draft the conservative/optimistic bullets Jonas requested and drop into the deck by Thu?

--Lauren

Date: Fri, 2 Jul 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: June checkpoint: propose OKR re-scope + QBR prep for BrightCore

Quick infra update — DGX inventory is constrained in our primary zone for the requested window. Options and trade-offs:

- Option A: Approve cloud burst on nv4 instances for 3 weeks (~$18k estimated) to run the benchmark matrix. Fastest path but increases variable cost.
- Option B: Use existing quantized-model pipeline + Redwood Optimize to run a narrower benchmark (2 extra days) and extrapolate full matrix. Lower cost but higher variance in estimate.
- Option C: Delay heavy kernels integration testing to mid-July when one DGX frees up (risk: pushes milestones).

If Org approves cloud burst, we can finish benchmarking by Jul 20 and update the QBR slides the same week. If not, recommend we accept the 30% re-scope and present the Optimize results (Option B) with clear caveats.

Attachment: DGX_request_form.pdf (filled with tentative dates).

-Marcus
Marcus Lin
Sr. Director, Infrastructure
marcus.lin@redwood.com
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 3 Jul 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: June checkpoint: propose OKR re-scope + QBR prep for BrightCore

Appreciate the fast responses. Decision summary and owners (for QBR and OKR communication):

Decision: Accept temporary re-scope for Serving runtime P99 target -> 30% this quarter. Proceed with autoscaler soft-launch limited to US-west region. If infra grants cloud burst, we'll run the full benchmark and publish an updated slide in the QBR deck; otherwise we'll use the Optimize-driven estimates with explicit caveats.

Action items (owners + deadlines):
- Marcus: Confirm DGX vs cloud burst by Mon Jul 6 EOD and provide firm cost number if cloud burst. (owner: marcus.lin)
- Marcus/Infra: If cloud burst approved, run benchmark matrix and deliver consolidated results by Jul 20. (owner: marcus.lin)
- Monica: Draft two BrightCore-facing bullets (conservative + optimistic) and add to QBR_slide_deck_v1.pdf by Thu Jul 9. (owner: monica.patel)
- Jonas/Product: Update OKR_rebaseline.xlsx with one-line rationale for each KR change and add a one-slide roadmap for the incremental milestones. (owner: jonas.weber / evelyn.hart)
- Lauren/Revenue Ops: Approve any cloud burst spend up to $20k for benchmarking or confirm budget hold. (owner: lauren.bishop)
- Steph: Prepare comms note for internal stakeholders and a short script for exec remarks in the QBR. (owner: stephanie.nguyen)

I'll create a concise QBR talking script and drop it in the Drive. Monica — loop in Sarah Patel from BrightCore only if we need to surface the re-scope before the QBR; otherwise we'll present the conservative phrasing in the meeting.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B-OKR-QBR-2026
DocuSign (if we need to sign a scheduling amendment for BrightCore): https://app.docusign.com/rooms/abc-123-qbr

Thanks — I'll present this in the leadership sync on Monday and sign off once Marcus confirms infra plan.
